title: 1990 Air Force low-voltage vacuum test of Biefeld-Brown

tellings.quote: For example, in 1990, the Air Force tested a Biefeld-Brown experiment in a vacuum, but they only used 19 kilovolts instead of the megavoltage Brown was using.

plain: Townsend Brown was an American inventor who said that very high voltages could produce a pushing force, an idea known as the Biefeld-Brown effect. The podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 1990 the US Air Force tested this effect in a vacuum, but used only 19,000 volts, while Brown had worked with millions of volts. Michels tells it to argue that the test was too weak to settle whether Brown was right.
